ai_prompt:
You are preparing a zip import pack for a school maths LMS.

ATTACHED: Ganita Prakash Grade 7 Part II — Chapter on Data Handling / statistics (PDF title may be "Connecting the Dots…").

TASK — produce TWO things:

1) questions.json — every gradable MCQ from the chapter
2) PNG images — crop/export each distinct chart, graph, dot plot, or data table figure from the PDF

ZIP LAYOUT:
  gp-class7-data-handling-mcqs.zip
  ├── questions.json
  ├── fig-dot-stories.png
  ├── fig-dot-palm-heights.png
  ├── fig-bar-onions.png
  ├── fig-bar-rockets.png
  ├── fig-table-heights-2019.png
  ├── fig-bar-cricket-overs.png
  ├── fig-bar-animal-speeds.png
  ├── fig-bar-superpower.png
  ├── fig-bar-jodhpur-temp.png
  ├── fig-bar-ev-registrations.png
  ├── fig-dot-pockets.png
  ├── fig-bar-skyscrapers.png
  ├── fig-dot-sudoku.png
  ├── fig-dot-grade5-heights.png
  └── (add more only if the PDF has additional distinct figures)

questions.json SHAPE (return ONLY this JSON object, no markdown fences):
{
  "questions": [
    {
      "topic": "Statistical questions | Mean | Median and outliers | Bar graphs | Dot plots | Reading data tables",
      "question": "Student-facing question text only (no 'see graph above')",
      "diagram_file": "fig-bar-onions.png",
      "table": {"headers": ["Col1", "Col2"], "rows": [["a", "b"]]},
      "chart": "Optional short backup description if useful",
      "options": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
      "correct_index": 0,
      "hint": "Theory/rules only — no final answer letter",
      "explanation": "Full working + Answer: B",
      "difficulty": "Easy|Medium|Hard"
    }
  ]
}

RULES:
- correct_index is 0-based (0 = first option)
- Exactly 4 options per question when possible
- INCLUDE: worked examples, inline exercises, numbered exercise sets, starred hard items
- EXCLUDE: pure discussion prompts, draw-only tasks, projects, puzzles without MCQ answers
- For ANY question that uses a figure in the PDF, set diagram_file to the matching PNG filename
- Multiple questions MAY share the same diagram_file (same chart reused)
- Tables in the PDF: either export as PNG (diagram_file) OR include full table JSON in "table" field (or both)
- Keep topic labels short and consistent (use the topic list above)
- Each question must be solvable from JSON + image together
- Image files: clean crops, readable labels, white background, PNG preferred, width ~800–1200px

DIAGRAM CATALOG (extract one PNG per row; reuse filename across all questions that use that figure):
| diagram_file | Figure in PDF |
| fig-dot-stories.png | Dot plot — short stories read by 15 students |
| fig-dot-palm-heights.png | Dot plot — date-palm tree heights |

Also include diagram_file for any table-only questions (e.g. cricket runs table Shubman/Yashasvi) as fig-table-cricket-runs.png if shown as a table in PDF.

OUTPUT FORMAT FOR YOU (the AI):
Step 1: Write complete questions.json
Step 2: Export/create each PNG listed above from the attached PDF
Step 3: Package into one .zip file

If you cannot create a binary zip in this chat, output questions.json in full and list each PNG as a separate downloadable file with the exact filename from diagram_catalog.

sample_questions.question: In which month was the price of onions in Wahapur the highest?
sample_questions.chart: Clustered column graph — monthly onion prices Yahapur (blue) vs Wahapur (red dotted). Scale ₹10 per unit.
sample_questions.hint: Find the tallest Wahapur bar on the graph.
sample_questions.explanation: Wahapur peak is October at ₹60/kg. Answer: B

sample_questions.question: What is the median number of short stories read?
sample_questions.hint: Order the 15 values and find the middle one.
sample_questions.explanation: Sorted data gives median 6. Answer: B

sample_questions.question: What is Shubman's total runs in the four matches shown?
sample_questions.hint: Add Shubman's runs across all four matches.
